metaDescription: Six leaf blowers rated 180 to 250 MPH, gas, cordless and corded, compared on nozzle speed, volume and weight for wet leaves and stuck debris.
expertTake: The Husqvarna 360BT is the best high-MPH blower for owners who want gas reliability, because 232 MPH is paired with 890 CFM and a real engine behind it. The BLACK+DECKER corded 180 MPH model is the value pick for a small yard near an outlet. Skip the category if your problem is moving big dry piles, because that is a volume job where speed adds little.
introParagraphs: Miles per hour measures how fast air leaves the nozzle, and that speed is what peels wet, matted or stuck-down debris off the ground. A fast, narrow jet breaks the grip of damp leaves, pine straw and grit in cracks where a slower, wider stream only rolls over the top.

Speed has costs. A high figure is almost always taken at the nozzle tip on the maker's bench, often on turbo, and a concentrator nozzle can raise speed by sacrificing volume. This guide reads each number against the volume, the power source and the weight it comes with.

products.name: Husqvarna 360BT gas backpack, 232 MPH, 890 CFM, 65.6cc
products.description:
The 360BT is the best-balanced blower here because it holds both numbers high at once: 232 MPH and 890 CFM. That pairing is the point. A machine that is merely fast leaves a pile where it is, and one that is merely voluminous rolls over matted leaves; this one does both. The X-Torque engine is the maker's low-emission two-stroke design, and the backpack layout puts the weight on your hips.

Compared with the Husqvarna 150BT in the same family, which uses a 51cc engine rated at 2.16 horsepower, the 360BT's 65.6cc displacement gives it a clear step up in sustained output. Against the ECHO PB-9010T at 220 MPH and 1110 CFM, it trades about 12 MPH of speed and a good deal of volume, which only matters on very large properties.

Expect gas ownership: premixed fuel, a clean air filter, a spark plug check each season and a drained tank before winter. Inspect the harness straps and the vibration mounts every autumn, because that is what keeps an hour-long session comfortable. Parts and service are easy to find through the maker's dealer network.
products.bestFor: Owners who want real speed and volume from a proven gas backpack.
pros: 232 MPH and 890 CFM together is a rare pairing
Backpack harness spreads weight to the hips
cons: Loud enough to need hearing protection
Heavy to store and lift into a truck

products.name: Vitaler 850 CFM, 250 MPH brushless cordless, 2 batteries
products.description:
Vitaler leads the cordless group on the headline numbers, 250 MPH with 850 CFM, from a brushless motor and a two-battery kit. The listing mentions light snow and dust as extra jobs, which hints at a focused, tube-style blower rather than a heavy-duty unit. The speed is aimed squarely at wet leaves and compacted debris on driveways.

The unknown is everything around the motor. The listing gives no battery capacity here, and the brand has no published tool platform, so you are buying a standalone kit. Compared with the Husqvarna 360BT it has the higher speed but no gas engine's sustained output, and compared with the EWZ at the same 250 MPH it has more volume at 850 against 750 CFM.

Treat batteries as the wear item. Keep them indoors in winter, rotate them, and avoid running them to zero on turbo, since deep discharges age lithium cells quickly. Clear the intake of grit after driveway work, because high-speed fans pull in fine dust that coats the vanes.
products.bestFor: Cordless owners who want the highest speed and volume without gas.
pros: 250 MPH is the top speed in this guide
cons: Battery capacity not stated on the listing

products.name: EWZ 750 CFM, 250 MPH cordless with a 10.0Ah pack
products.description:
EWZ matches the Vitaler's 250 MPH and gets there with a 20,000 rpm brushless motor and one big 10.0Ah battery. Its claimed 150 minutes is a low-speed runtime, so plan on a fraction of that when you hold the trigger at high output. That single pack is both its strength, because it lasts, and its weakness, because there is no second pack to swap.

At 750 CFM it gives up 100 CFM to the Vitaler, which is a modest gap. If your work is mostly stubborn patches, such as wet leaves on a patio or debris in gravel joints, you will not miss the volume. If you clear lawns of dry leaves, the Vitaler or the Husqvarna 360BT will move more material per pass.

Ownership mostly means looking after one battery. Store it at partial charge, away from freezing, and never leave it in a hot vehicle. A 10.0Ah pack is a significant replacement cost, so read the warranty period before you buy.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want 250 MPH from one long-running battery.
pros: 250 MPH matches the fastest cordless here
cons: Runtime claim applies to low settings
Expensive single pack if it fails

products.name: ECHO PB-9010T 79.9cc gas backpack, 220 MPH, 1110 CFM
products.description:
Here the speed is secondary to the engine: 79.9cc is a large two-stroke that drives 1110 CFM, the most volume in this guide. The 220 MPH sits below the Husqvarna 360BT's 232, but with this much volume behind the jet it keeps its grip on wet material better than the number suggests. The tube-mounted throttle lets you ride output without reaching for the engine.

It is built for large properties and for operators who spend an hour or more at a time with the harness on. That also means it is the heaviest, loudest and thirstiest machine in the roundup. Use it for open acreage and commercial-style cleanup, not for a patio.

Plan on the full two-stroke routine: premix fuel at the right ratio, a clean air filter each session, spark plug inspection, and a drained tank before winter. Check the throttle cable and the harness for wear annually.
products.bestFor: Large yards where volume and speed both matter.
pros: 220 MPH with a strong air column

products.name: SCHTUMPA 1200W brushless cordless, 700 CFM, 200 MPH
products.description:
SCHTUMPA is the middle path: 200 MPH and 700 CFM from a 1200W brushless motor, with two batteries in the kit. It sits 50 MPH below the Vitaler and EWZ, which you will notice on stuck wet leaves, but it holds up for general lawn cleanup. The maker claims up to 160 minutes of runtime, which like every cordless claim is a low-setting figure.

The 1200W rating is a motor power claim, not a measure of air power at the nozzle, so do not compare it with gas horsepower. It is an ordinary, practical cordless kit for a mid-size yard where you want speed that beats a basic 150 MPH blower without paying for a platform tool.

Care is routine. Keep the packs charged and stored indoors, clean the intake grille, and look for cracks in the nozzle after dropping it.
products.bestFor: Mid-size yards wanting solid speed at a moderate tier.
pros: 200 MPH is a good mid-range speed
cons: 50 MPH slower than the 250 MPH models
1200W is a motor figure, not output

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 7-Amp corded blower, 180 MPH, 180 CFM
products.description:
This is the entry point: a 7 amp corded blower that makes 180 MPH and 180 CFM. The speed is respectable for a plug-in model, but the volume is a fraction of the 850 CFM Vitaler. It is a tool for patios, decks and driveways rather than lawns.

Its advantage is that it never runs down and weighs very little, so it is the one you will pick up for a five-minute job. The limitation is range: a heavy gauge extension cord is mandatory, and a thin one will starve the motor.

Upkeep is minimal: clear the intake, inspect the cord, and store it dry. That low-maintenance profile is the reason it remains useful.
products.bestFor: Small yards, decks and patios within cord reach.
pros: 180 MPH from a simple corded blower
Lowest cost tier in this guide

buyingCriteria.explanation: MPH is how hard the air hits, CFM is how much of it there is. The Husqvarna 360BT at 232 MPH and 890 CFM has both, while the BLACK+DECKER at 180 MPH and 180 CFM has speed with little volume behind it. A fast jet with low volume will lift a wet leaf but not move the pile. Aim for at least 600 CFM if you want speed to be useful across a lawn.

Air speed is normally taken at the nozzle opening on the maker's bench, and often with a concentrator nozzle fitted. Speed falls off sharply within a meter of the tip. The Vitaler and EWZ both claim 250 MPH, but you should expect an effective working speed much lower at arm's length.

Boost modes raise speed for a short burst, and the quoted maximum is often only available on turbo. Cordless blowers drain their packs quickly at that setting. Check what the middle dial gives, because that is the speed you will actually use for most of a session.

A gas engine like the Husqvarna's 65.6cc holds its speed until the tank is empty, while a cordless motor sags as the pack drains. The SCHTUMPA's 1200W motor and 160 minute claim apply at low settings. If you need speed over a long session, gas or a two-pack kit is safer.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Weight at the end of your arm
buyingCriteria.explanation: A handheld blower that is fast but heavy gets abandoned. The BLACK+DECKER is the lightest here, while the backpack Husqvarna and ECHO spread weight onto the hips. Think about the longest session you do and match the carry method to it.

A round nozzle concentrates the jet and a flat one sweeps a wide path. Concentrators raise speed at the expense of volume. A blower with both nozzles, as many dual-tube models offer, handles pavement and lawn better than one with a fixed tip.

specDecoder.meaning: The speed of air leaving the nozzle. Higher speed breaks the grip of wet leaves and debris on the ground.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Vitaler and EWZ both claim 250 MPH, but only measured at the tip.

specDecoder.meaning: The volume of air moved per minute. It decides how much leaf mass you can push in one pass.
specDecoder.watchFor: The corded BLACK+DECKER at 180 CFM moves a fraction of the 890 CFM Husqvarna.

specDecoder.meaning: A motor without carbon brushes, which runs cooler and wears more slowly. It is common on better cordless tools.
specDecoder.watchFor: Vitaler, EWZ and SCHTUMPA are brushless; the corded BLACK+DECKER is a basic brushed design.

specDecoder.meaning: Engine size, a better guide to power than gross horsepower claims. The larger it is, the more air the blower can move.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Husqvarna 360BT at 65.6cc and the ECHO at 79.9cc outrun the 51cc 150BT.

specDecoder.meaning: How long a pack lasts, usually on the lowest speed setting. Real use at high speed is much shorter.
specDecoder.watchFor: EWZ claims 150 minutes and SCHTUMPA 160, both low-speed figures.

howWeEvaluated.title: Speed against volume
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each blower's MPH in the context of its CFM. The Husqvarna 360BT's 232 MPH with 890 CFM scored higher than the BLACK+DECKER's 180 and 180. A fast jet without volume was marked down.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sustained output
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on the spec sheet, we separated claims that apply to turbo from those that apply to the mid dial. Gas engines and two-battery kits were treated as better at sustaining speed. Single-pack runtime claims were discounted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and carry
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed backpack against handheld designs by the length of session each suits. A fast blower that tires the user is less effective. The lightweight corded model was credited for short jobs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership burden
howWeEvaluated.description: Fuel and spark plugs for gas, battery care for cordless, and cords for plug-in each carry a different upkeep load. We also looked at brand support and parts availability. Dealer networks counted for the Husqvarna and ECHO.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value tier
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared relative price tiers to speed delivered, from the lowest-cost corded model up to the gas backpacks. Extra cost was credited only when a spec gap justified it.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: The Husqvarna 360BT and ECHO PB-9010T hold their speed until the tank is empty and refuel in a minute. They are louder, need premix fuel and require seasonal care. They suit heavy, long jobs.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: The Vitaler, EWZ and SCHTUMPA are quiet, start instantly and need no fuel. Their speed sags as the battery drains, and turbo is brief. They suit short, frequent jobs.

howToChoose.note: Choose gas for acreage and long sessions; choose cordless for mid-size yards.

rows: Fast and light for quick jobs
Long sessions with weight on hips

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Air speed above 200 MPH with at least 600 CFM behind it, because wet leaves stick to turf and need a hard jet to peel loose. Wet leaves weigh far more than dry ones, so expect the real result to be lower than the spec sheet.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Vitaler at 250 MPH and 850 CFM is the best cordless choice, and the Husqvarna 360BT at 232 MPH and 890 CFM is the best gas choice. The BLACK+DECKER at 180 CFM lacks the volume to carry heavy wet leaves.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You clear heavy wet leaves regularly or work more than half an hour at a time. The Husqvarna 360BT and Vitaler both pay for themselves in time saved.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your cleanup is patios and driveways in small sections. The BLACK+DECKER or SCHTUMPA handle that without a high price.

maintenance.why: High-speed fans draw in grit and matted leaf fragments. A blocked intake overheats the motor and cuts speed.
Cracks and loose joints leak air and cut velocity. Replace a damaged nozzle.
Fresh premix, a clean filter and a fresh spark plug keep the Husqvarna and ECHO at full speed. Stale fuel is the top no-start cause.
Store at partial charge indoors and avoid draining to zero. Lithium packs age fast when hot or empty.
A nicked cord is a shock hazard and wastes power. Replace damaged cords at once.

faq.a: No. Speed helps lift stuck debris, but without volume it leaves piles in place. Look for a blower with both, such as the Husqvarna 360BT.

faq.q: How much does a high-MPH blower cost?
faq.a: The corded BLACK+DECKER is at the lowest tier, cordless kits sit in the middle, and the gas backpacks are at the top. Pay more for volume and support. Prices change, so check listings.
Brushless motors and gas engines with regular servicing last for years. Batteries are the shorter-lived part. Warranty and parts support matter more than the speed.
It is a nozzle-tip measurement taken on the maker's bench. The air slows quickly as it leaves the tip, so effective speed at a working distance is far lower.

faq.q: Is a high-MPH blower safe for flower beds?
faq.a: A fast jet can strip mulch and bruise plants. Use a lower dial or a wider nozzle near beds. Variable speed matters here.
Gas models are the loudest, and a high-speed fan is noisy even on cordless. Ear protection is wise on turbo. Cordless is the quieter option.
